problem: "Clockwise when you look along +x" is ambiguous. If a student reads it as standing at the origin and looking in the +x direction, then +y is up and +z is to the right, so the negative moment would appear anticlockwise, the opposite of what is written. The stated sense is right only for a viewer on the positive x side looking back at the origin.
fix: Write: "16 N·m clockwise when viewed from the positive x-axis looking toward the origin, i.e. looking in the −x direction." Use the same wording in the answer line and in quiz Q6.

problem: "A force at the same distance but more perpendicular gives a larger moment" is unclear about which distance. If the distance means the perpendicular distance d, then M = F d is unchanged and the sentence contradicts the formula.
fix: Say: "A force applied at the same point A but directed more nearly perpendicular to OA has a larger perpendicular distance d = OA sinθ, and so gives a larger moment."
